name: openGym
cost: Free. The optional AI coach uses your own AI provider key
works_with: Docker with Compose on your own server (amd64 or arm64 images). Use it from a phone or laptop browser, or the Android APK
short: A self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker with guided workouts, synced across your devices behind passkey login.
what: openGym is a workout tracker you run on your own box. You plan routines over a library of 1,324 exercises, run guided sessions with a rest timer and pre-filled weights, and log sets and body weight. Data stays as JSON files in a ./data folder on your host and syncs between your devices.
who: People who lift and want their training log on their own server instead of a subscription app, and who are comfortable running Docker. If you only want a phone app with no server, the README points to a standalone Android APK. Skip it if you don't want to look after a server or set up HTTPS.
needs: About 140 MB of disk for exercise media, downloaded once on first start
HTTPS on a domain if you want to sign in with passkeys from your phone. The self-hosting guide covers Cloudflare Tunnel, Caddy, Traefik and nginx
Optional: your own provider key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama included) for the AI coach

steps.title: Create your settings file
steps.text: All configuration lives in .env. RP_ID and ORIGIN must match the address you serve it from.

steps.title: Pull the prebuilt images and start it
steps.text: Skip the pull to build from source instead.
steps.code:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

steps.title: Open it and create a profile
steps.text: Go to http://localhost:8080 and tap Create profile.

steps.title: Set up HTTPS for your phone
steps.text: Passkeys from a phone need HTTPS on a domain. Follow docs/SELF_HOSTING.md, which also covers HTTPS on a LAN and Kubernetes.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Open http://localhost:8080, tap Create profile, and load one of the four starter plans (Push/Pull/Legs, Upper/Lower, Full Body, 5x5). Or try the in-browser demo first: https://opengym.duarte-santos.ch/demo/

watch: The first start downloads about 140 MB of exercise media from a third-party source. The README says those images and animations are not covered by the AGPL and their ownership is disputed, so don't reuse them without clearing it with the rights holder.

The README says the default install calls no AI service and has no telemetry. The AI coach and MCP server are off by default. If you turn the coach on, your training data goes to the AI provider you configure, with your key.
Guest use ("Continue without account") is on by default. Set ALLOW_GUEST=0 and consider INVITE_ONLY if the instance is reachable from the internet.
Back up the ./data folder. It holds every profile, workout and the session signing key.
Login trouble is almost always an RP_ID/ORIGIN mismatch in .env, per the README.
AGPL-3.0: if you run a modified version as a network service, you must offer that version's source.
